quest.title: The Five Colors' True Form
quest.rewards_formatted: Crown of Insight x1, Mora x20000, Yashiro Commission Gift x1

chapter.num: True Tales of the Violet Garden: Act IV
chapter.title: The Palace, Dyed in Black

talks.objective: Return to The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Hello {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo, why is the portrait of Kuronushi all covered up? Paimon wants to see what your Kuronushi portrait looks like.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Don't worry, the unveiling ceremony will be starting shortly. You'll see what it looks like then.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I will say that I'm most satisfied with this particular work. I even made a special trip to see someone in order to complete it. They gave me some very valuable suggestions.

choices.text: Things are starting to sound pretty mysterious.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Hehe, is that so? Anyway, there is still time before the ceremony, you may have a look around the venue first.

choices.text: Sounds pretty suspicious if you ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, it's a pleasure to see you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did today's signing go as planned?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Indeed, it did. Thanks to you, the signing event went off without a hitch! And I must say, the readers seemed most satisfied.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Xingqiu... Is it just Paimon, or are you on the lookout for something?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: You aren't mistaken. Though I'm ashamed to admit it, but in fact, I have been on the watch for tourists from Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: After all, I came to Inazuma under the pretext of evaluating a potential investment. If an acquaintance were to see me sitting here, then there would be no way to hide the truth from my father.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Fortunately, the crowds of readers that came flocking over have kept the usual tourists at bay.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh, I should mention, Xu is also unaware of the real purpose of my trip. If you happen to meet him, please, remember to keep it secret.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we've got you covered.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Then please accept my thanks in advance. I'm sorry that I can't chat long, there are still readers waiting in line.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I'll see you later at the unveiling ceremony for Kuronushi's portrait.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Greetings Traveler, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Ayato! We finally get to see the busiest person of all.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Yes, there were many things which required my attention these past few days.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Fortunately, the Irodori Festival is proceeding smoothly. The Tri-Commission cooperated closely to prepare this festival, so at long last, I can take a break today.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Brother and I are very grateful for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hmm, Thoma sure is taking his sweet time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, you're waiting for Thoma?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes, today is one of the rare occasions when brother isn't busy. I was going to buy some books but he said he wanted to come along, "his treat." However, he forgot his wallet at home, so he asked Thoma to go back and fetch it for him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't think Ayato could ever be forgetful like that.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Hehe, brother always works diligently, and it's rare for him to ever put his duties to the side and relax.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: So, Thoma and I really cherish such moments when he's forgetful.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Well, hello everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you two doing together!? Don't think we didn't see you two chatting up a storm just now. The moment we came over, you stopped talking.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Is that so? I'm afraid you're just overthinking things.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: We were merely discussing wine and food, I'm sure you two wouldn't be interested.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ahem, speaking of good sides with sake, I personally prefer fried tofu...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, forget it. Even if those two are plotting something, they'd still never let us know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kazuha, what are you doing here? Why aren't you at the festival?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I came here to take in the sea breeze. Such a bustling atmosphere is never really to my liking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you really alright, Kazuha?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Heh, I knew you were still worried about me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Thank you, but please don't worry. The things I said in front of everyone weren't just pretty-sounding excuses.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Look, see this familiar harbor in front of us? Before, you could sit here all day without seeing a single ship pass through. Instead, all you would see were soldiers from the Kanjou Commission guarding against possible intruders.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: But now, it's become a bustling place.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Not only are foreigners coming to Inazuma again, but traffic between here and Watatsumi Island has also been picking up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Inazuma's already started to change, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I was thinking... In some ways, each and every one of us are similar to this country.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: It might take a different amount of time for different people, but there will inevitably come a day when each person can let go of their burdens.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: And when they finally let go, they are free to follow the wind as they please.

talks.objective: Return to The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Everyone, welcome to the Magnificent Irodori Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Today, we have ushered in the final stage of our festival.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: And now, we will reveal the final portrait of The Five Kasen — Kuronushi, which was done by none other than our guest artist from Mondstadt, Calx.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon has no idea what Albedo's portrait looks like... Ugh, this is so nerve-racking!

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Let's all count down together! Three, two, one!

dialogues.speaker: Guest
dialogues.text: Huh? What's this? This piece depicts nothing but a background!

dialogues.speaker: Guest
dialogues.text: I suppose Calx must have forgotten to include the character.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Ahem. Uh, let's hear some words from Calx himself regarding the creative process behind this piece.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hello everyone. First, I would like to say that it was an honor to be invited to create the portraits of The Five Kasen.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The Five Kasen are legendary figures from ancient Inazuma, famous for their works of poetry. As time passed, poems were composed about them, and they became the subjects of many stories.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I learned from existing sources about those stories that the character of Kuronushi is the deepest and most differing of The Five Kasen.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Moreover, Kuronushi lacks a dedicated chapter among the stories. It's as if he is a "behind-the-scenes role" of The Five Kasen.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Perhaps we can assume that every creator had a different understanding of Kuronushi. So, in the same way, I also wanted to leave this character to everyone's own imagination.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: After all, the Irodori Festival is a place for everyone to express their minds through creative works.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, that's Albedo for ya! His super logical explanation is sure to win everyone's approval.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it seems that our adventures at the Irodori Festival have come to a close, hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wh—What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Ohhh! Right, we still haven't figured out who left those stories of The Five Kasen for us to find.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, I have an inkling of who it might be.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? C'mon then, who is it? Tell Paimon!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: First, it's someone that knows every one of us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that makes sense... Otherwise, there'd be no way to give the right paper to the right person every time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Also, they are connected with the Kaedehara Clan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, even though they were using stories to hint us toward Xingqiu's troubles, the real goal was to lead us to solve the secrets of the Kaedehara Clan...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *gasp* Paimon gets it now! Well, at least Paimon thinks she knows...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go! We'll get to the bottom of this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayato! You're the one behind the stories of The Five Kasen!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, don't you think you overdid it a little, leading all your friends on a wild hunt like that!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Haha. As it just so happens, one of the reasons I'm here today is to explain the details behind this "wild hunt."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, Paimon wants to see how you'll explain yourself out of this one.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: First of all, the start of this whole incident was due to mere happenstance. You see, Lady Yae happened to catch sight of Xingqiu and the editor carrying the books away one night. She thought it was interesting, so she asked me to tease them a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? So it was Miko after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knew it! This thing had Miko written all over it...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: That's right, but using the story of The Five Kasen to guide you to the Kaedehara family's secrets was my personal touch.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: As for my roundabout approach... Well, that was something which I had no choice but to do.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You had no choice?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Yes. Due to a certain incident that occurred earlier, I happened to notice the bonsai plants left behind by Kaedehara Yoshinori, as well as the blank papers hidden inside.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I knew there was more than meets the eye regarding those papers, but it took me some time to figure out the secret behind the ink, the kind that would only appear when exposed to water.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: What Kaedehara Yoshinori said in the letter is very important for both the Kamisato Clan and the descendants of the Kaedehara Clan, especially Kazuha.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The Kaedehara Clan used to be subordinates of the Kamisato Clan. It was my ancestors who were unable to protect them all those years ago. So now, this obligation fell on my shoulders.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Although he has the right to know the truth, the closer he draws to things hidden out of sight, the closer he also draws to danger. I had to confirm whether Kazuha has both the will and ability to be privy to the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Of course, I could outright tell him the truth that I had discovered, but maybe he doesn't have the will that's required. In that case, the truth would only become a burden to him.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: If he lacks the ability, then he wouldn't be able to find the truth in the first place. In which case, it would be better to keep him away from danger altogether.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Kaedehara Yoshinori left his message in a roundabout way precisely for this reason.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: For a long time, I yearned for a suitable opportunity to convey this matter, right up until the night when "A Legend of Sword" was smuggled away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But why was everyone else involved, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, it wasn't only Kazuha. You brought all the rest of us into this plan of yours!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I figured you would ask this question eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I merely saw that this matter would be of value to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: And more importantly, I hoped that while Kazuha and Ayaka were looking for the answers together, they would have some reliable friends by their side.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Reliable friends who would be willing to protect them and make measured decisions. Friends who would spare no effort to lend a helping hand in times of trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Because it is also very likely that you will face the same enemy together in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So who is Kunikuzushi?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: You already know the answer deep down inside, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The answer is actually hidden in the portrait of Kuronushi.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: When there is no one else near the portrait, you can confirm with your own eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: As for the means of revealing that answer... well, you have used it many times before.

talks.objective: Return to The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's getting pretty late, so nobody else is around now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Ayato must have been telling us to splash water on the portrait, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *gasp* It's... It's the Balladeer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he was the one behind the trouble all those years ago!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: When there is no one else near the portrait, you can confirm with your own eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: As for the means of revealing that answer... well, you have used it many times before.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Also, there's one last thing that we must discuss.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I mentioned earlier that the occurrence of "a certain incident" made me notice the bonsai plants. I wish to tell you of that incident now.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It was just after the Shogun announced the abolition of the Sakoku Decree. I heard that something had happened at the Tenryou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: They had discovered signs that someone had entered the warehouse storing the commission's articles of evidence and confiscated items. But, nothing was stolen.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I felt something unusual about that incident, so I told Kujou Sara of the Tenryou Commission to treat it as if nothing happened. She was not to increase the guard or relocate the warehouse contents.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: In the meantime, I sent a member of the Shuumatsuban to keep watch over the warehouse. And sure enough, someone was sneaking in and rummaging through the belongings of the Kaedehara Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, he was also looking for...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Heh, I let him search for a while, but in the end, he found nothing. Soon after, he had to leave Inazuma by boat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why didn't you send someone to catch him?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hehe. The best way to protect a secret is to treat it as if it doesn't exist, is it not? Besides, the identity of this person is not hard to guess.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: After he left Inazuma, I carefully checked the Kaedehara Clan's belongings one by one, and eventually discovered the papers in the hidden compartment of the flower pot.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I am certain that the papers are the secret which the infiltrator sought to find, though he couldn't confirm whether this secret existed at all.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: So, now on to my final question...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Which part of Kaedehara Yoshinori's experiences was the secret that needed to be protected?

choices.text: That Kaedehara Yoshinori knew that the family was framed?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hahaha, I don't have an answer to this question at present, so I'll leave it to your future self.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: As for now, please enjoy yourselves at the Irodori Festival.

choices.text: That Kaedehara Yoshinori knew that the culprit was named Kunikuzushi?
That Kaedehara Yoshinori was spared by his opponent?

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: The release event has been a huge success. It's all thanks to you, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Satomi
dialogues.text: I heard that not only is Zhenyu heir to a Liyue merchant family, but he also created the entire novel without ever telling his family. Come to think of it, that's quite similar to the plot in the novel.

dialogues.speaker: Satomi
dialogues.text: Hmm... Perhaps next time we should try to write a story about a novelist based on Zhenyu.

dialogues.speaker: Kadenokouji Kenzaburou
dialogues.text: Lots of people came to buy books today. Though the signing process wasn't difficult, after so many copies, I can barely lift my hand.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You should have a look around the venue first, today will likely be the busiest day of the Irodori Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me. You should go enjoy the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh, are you asking about the one who left the stories of The Five Kasen? Hehe, I do happen to know their true identity.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But things may be a little more complicated than you think.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Are you discussing the person who left The Five Kasen stories? They are indeed a meticulous person who's good at reading the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, in fact, before doing the portrait of Kuronushi, I visited the person who left those stories and confirmed a few things.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I think my current approach to this portrait is the most correct one. After all, there are some things that are better left obscure and out of the public eye.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: The person who left behind the stories of The Five Kasen probably chose to do so for Kaedehara's sake.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: After all, if they wanted to simply tell me what happened, there'd be far easier ways of doing it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: To be honest, I am very grateful to the one who left those stories for us to find. This journey allowed me to uncover the truth behind my family.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: And, I am also very fortunate to have you to accompany me and find the answers.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The one who left the stories of The Five Kasen? Haha, I'm afraid you guessed wrong, Paimon. It wasn't me~

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Really!? Paimon thought for sure you'd be the sneaky and tricky one!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Haha, but seeing as you stumbled upon me, you aren't far from finding that person now.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Because other than me, there's only one person left.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: (Xingqiu currently seems to be carefully signing books for his readers. His penmanship is quite smooth. Even though the stamp designed by Albedo is not very complicated, he must have practiced for quite a long time just to make his readers happy...)

dialogues.speaker: The Kamisato Siblings
dialogues.text: (The two people talk about various things regarding the Irodori Festival while they wait for Thoma. You can hear snatches of their conversation: "Brother, even if Thoma is here, you cannot simply forget to bring your purse"...)

dialogues.speaker: Miko and Venti
dialogues.text: (Miko and Venti are drinking and chatting in a corner. The empty bottles are starting to pile up at an alarming rate... But it seems that they've really been discussing the best sides to go with sake this whole time.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Today's the final stage of the Irodori Festival. Not only will there be Xingqiu's signing event, but Albedo's painting of Kuronushi will also be unveiled.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a stroll through the festival venue, maybe we'll find everyone there.
